title: Epidemiological Modeling of Jailbreak Spread: R0 for Prompt Exploits

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The analogy between jailbreak propagation and epidemiology is creative and the R0 concept could inform patching strategy. However, the core assumption that jailbreak variants propagate through a semantic similarity graph is speculative and may not reflect real-world dynamics.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: SIR models are mathematically straightforward and well-documented. Embedding similarity graphs are easy to build. However, generating meaningful jailbreak mutation graphs and calibrating realistic parameters requires domain expertise beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The core deliverable (simulate SIR on a jailbreak graph, estimate R0, test hub patching) is reasonably bounded, though building the mutation graph and calibrating parameters adds scope.

novelty.reasoning: Web search found no published research applying epidemiological models (SIR, R0 estimation) to jailbreak prompt propagation. Research on jailbreak prompt datasets (Shen et al., CCS 2024, 15,140 prompts including 1,405 jailbreaks from Reddit/Discord/websites) documents that prompts evolve 'similarly to malware strains' but does not formalize this with epidemiological models. LLM-Fuzzer (USENIX Security 2024) generates mutation-based variants but does not model propagation dynamics. The semantic similarity graph + SIR model + R0 estimation + hub patching strategy is a novel interdisciplinary contribution, though the practical utility depends on whether the epidemiological analogy holds for jailbreak dynamics.
